related_questions.question: What is the introduction of a heart attack?
related_questions.snippet: A heart attack, also known as a myocardial infarction, happens when the flow of blood that brings oxygen to a part of your heart muscle suddenly becomes blocked. Your heart can't get enough oxygen. If blood flow is not restored quickly, the heart muscle will begin to die. Heart attacks are very common.

related_questions.question: What is the introduction of the heart?
related_questions.snippet: The heart consists of four chambers organized into two pumps (right and left) to provide blood flow to the systemic and pulmonary circulations. The right atrium receives deoxygenated blood from the entire body except for the lungs (the systemic circulation) via the superior and inferior vena cavae.

text_blocks.snippet: A heart attack occurs when a coronary artery becomes blocked, preventing blood flow to the heart muscle. This blockage deprives the heart muscle of oxygen, which can cause part of the heart muscle to die if not treated quickly.
snippet_highlighted_words: occurs when a coronary artery becomes blocked, preventing blood flow to the heart muscle

text_blocks.snippet: Key points about a heart attack:

list.title: Cause:
list.snippet: Usually due to the buildup of plaque in the coronary arteries, which narrows the arteries and can eventually lead to a complete blockage.

list.title: Symptoms:
list.snippet: Classic symptoms include chest pain or discomfort, pressure or tightness in the chest, pain radiating to the arm, shoulder, or jaw, shortness of breath, sweating, nausea, and dizziness. However, some people may experience no or only mild symptoms.

list.title: Medical emergency:
list.snippet: If you suspect you or someone else is having a heart attack, call 9-1-1 immediately.
